title: Diwali outfit ideas for men
description: Diwali outfits for men: traditional kurta and modern shirt options, three budgets with real brands, and what to wear to puja and parties.
intro: Diwali is the one festival where almost every man wears a kurta. You have two good options. The traditional one is a silk or cotton kurta with a pyjama. The modern one is a plain shirt with a Nehru jacket, or a fitted kurta with dark jeans. Both work. Pick one and wear it well. This guide shows what to buy at three budgets, what to wear to puja and to the party, and what not to waste money on.

sections.heading: Traditional or modern
sections.body: Traditional is a kurta and pyjama in a jewel tone: maroon, navy, emerald, mustard, or deep blue. Silk blends and cotton silk look rich in puja photos. Modern is a short kurta in cotton or linen with dark jeans and juttis, or a plain shirt with a printed Nehru jacket. If your family is traditional, go traditional for the puja and modern for the evening party. Fit decides the look. A kurta that ends mid-thigh and fits the shoulder looks sharp.
tips: Traditional: silk blend kurta, churidar or straight pyjama, juttis.
Modern: short kurta or plain shirt, dark jeans, Nehru jacket.
Colours: maroon, navy, emerald, mustard, deep blue. Skip pastel and black for puja.

sections.heading: Climate note
sections.body: Diwali falls in October or November. North India is cool at night, so carry a jacket or shawl. In Mumbai, Chennai, and Bangalore the days stay warm. Choose cotton silk over pure silk. You will stand near diyas and lights, so avoid synthetic fabrics that melt or catch. Pick breathable cotton and linen blends.

sections.heading: Three looks by budget
sections.body: Prices below are approximate. Manyavar and Fabindia carry the best festive kurtas for men. Both are on Myntra and Ajio.

looks.name: Home puja, tight budget
pieces: Fabindia or Souled Store cotton kurta, about ₹1,300
looks.budget_inr: under 1,500 for the kurta and pyjama
looks.why: Solid colour in a rich tone. Simple is fine when the family photo is the point.

looks.name: Family party, mid range
pieces: Manyavar kurta set in maroon or navy, about ₹3,500
looks.why: Manyavar gives a clean silk-blend finish. It also arrives well fitted from Myntra.

looks.name: Evening party, upper range
pieces: Manyavar or Rare Rabbit Nehru jacket, about ₹4,500
looks.budget_inr: 4,000 to 10,000 for the jacket and kurta
looks.why: A printed jacket over a solid kurta looks like you planned it. It also works at weddings.

tips: Buy the jacket before the kurta. It works with three kurtas.
Get the kurta hemmed or taken in once. It costs about ₹300.

sections.heading: Events across Diwali
sections.body: Dhanteras shopping needs a comfortable cotton kurta and good walking shoes. Puja needs a traditional kurta in a rich colour. Card night needs a soft kurta or a plain shirt you can sit in for hours. Bhai Dooj needs a fresh kurta, often coordinated with siblings. Do not wear heavy perfume near diyas.

sections.heading: How to get the fit right
sections.body: Fit is the cheapest upgrade you can buy. A kurta should end at mid-thigh or just below the hip for a modern look. The shoulder seam should sit on the edge of your shoulder, not halfway down your arm. Sleeves should reach the wrist bone. If you cannot lift your arms to touch a diya, the armholes are too tight. Most tailors in India take in a kurta in a day for about ₹300. Do it. Then press the kurta the night before. A creased silk blend reads as tired, even when the colour is perfect. Finally, check the pyjama length. It should touch the top of the shoe, with a small bunch at most. A pyjama that drags on the floor ruins a good kurta in every photo.

sections.heading: What to stop buying
sections.body: Stop buying a new kurta every year in the same colour. Stop buying glittery fabric that itches. Stop buying pointed party shoes you cannot walk in. Add one jacket and one pair of juttis instead.

sections.heading: Grooming in one line
sections.body: Get a haircut before the festival, oil or beard balm for the beard, and light cologne.

faq.q: What should men wear on Diwali?
faq.a: A kurta and pyjama in a rich colour is the classic choice. A short kurta with dark jeans or a plain shirt with a Nehru jacket works well for the modern look.

faq.q: What colour should men avoid on Diwali?
faq.a: Avoid all black and plain white for puja. Choose maroon, navy, emerald, mustard, or deep blue instead.

faq.q: Where can men buy a good Diwali kurta online?
faq.a: Myntra and Ajio stock Manyavar, Fabindia, and Raymond kurtas. Order early. Popular sizes sell out two weeks before Diwali.

faq.q: Can I wear a kurta with jeans on Diwali?
faq.a: Yes. Use a short kurta with dark jeans and juttis. Avoid long kurtas with jeans. They look unbalanced.
